summary: Steel fire tower in Chattooga County, Georgia, run by the Georgia Forestry Commission; NHLR-registered 2017. Build date disputed (1930s vs 1956); no staffing or access sources found.

facts.design: steel tower with six-by-six-foot metal cab

events.note: NHLR gives the decade only: built in the 1930s to watch Taylors Ridge. Sources disagree with the 1956 entry below.
Forest Lookouts, quoting an Armuchee Ranger District history, gives 1956; the NHLR page says built in the 1930s. Sources disagree.
Registered August 28, 2017 as US 1239, GA 23; nominated by Justin Peel

evidence.supports: location: within the Chattahoochee National Forest
administered by the Georgia Forestry Commission
U.S. Forest Service listed as cooperator
NHLR gives build date as the 1930s, to watch Taylors Ridge
evidence.quote: This lookout was built in the 1930s to watch Taylors Ridge and the surrounding area.

evidence.supports: Chattooga County entry is a Georgia Forestry Commission tower
constructed in 1956 by the Georgia Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: This fire tower was constructed in 1956 by the state's Georgia Forestry Commission.

evidence.supports: steel tower, six by six foot metal cab, 60 feet tall
evidence.quote: The steel tower had a six foot by six foot metal cab and is 60 feet in height.

evidence.supports: the quoted history is the Armuchee Ranger District history
evidence.quote: History of the Armuchee Ranger District

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says built in the 1930s; Forest Lookouts quotes a 1956 construction date. The story reports both and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: NHLR registration date, registry numbers, elevation and agency match. Brief's status 'standing' is not stated by either source, so it is left out of facts. The 1956 date rests on one hobbyist list quoting an Armuchee Ranger District history that I did not locate. Georgia towers list (tnlandforms.us/gatowers.html) gives 1529 ft, against NHLR's 1,540 ft; not cited in the story. Do not confuse with the Walker County 'high point' entry on that list (GA238), a different tower. Two web searches and no staffing, fire, closure or access sources found. Access level left unset; visit status unknown.
